category: other: mug tipped in the grip during placement - pushed into the narrow dispensing slot, rotated in the fingers and released lying on its side; button then never attempted
what_happened: Scene: layout 7, tall narrow machine CoffeeMachine039 (dark front panel with a round gold button, a narrow dispensing slot below), grey mug_9 on the upper shelf. Stage 0: first close on air 124, grasp 140, mug carried down and held upright in front of the slot at 236. 252-280 the gripper pushed the mug into the slot; it hit the machine and rotated in the fingers (tipped >45 deg from 278). It was released 306 lying on its side in the slot, 0.0255 m from the pour site (0.0259 m 2 s later, tilt 82.6 deg to the end). Officially stage 0 is complete from 367 (no upright test). Stage 1: the gripper rose (360-440, wrist looks down on the tipped mug), backed away and from ~500 to 1200 hovered 30-60 cm from the machine, looking at it and the toaster. It never touched the machine (no machine contact in the whole episode).
causal_chain: mug pushed into the narrow slot 252-280 -> mug tips over in the gripper (278), released on its side 306 -> official stage 0 counts it as placed (367) -> policy never approaches the button, hovers 500-1200 -> timeout
self_recovery: none: no attempt to right the mug and no attempt at the button.
official_criterion_notes: Stage 0 is complete 367-1200 with the mug lying on its side (tilt 82.6 deg): the official check has no upright test. Had the button been pressed, the episode would have scored a success with a toppled mug. Officially only stage 1 failed; physically the mug placement failed.
uncertain_about: Whether the tipped mug is why the policy never went to the button (the same machine in success s28, with an upright mug, got a button approach ~180 steps after release). The exact contact that tipped the mug is hidden by the gripper at 264-288.
